# Detection rule catalogue

Every finding is produced by one of these deterministic, versioned rules. Severity describes impact; confidence describes how directly the packets prove the conclusion. The two are rated separately.

| Rule | Version | Category | Default severity | Title |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TCP-001 | 1.2.0 | tcp | high | Connection attempts receive no SYN-ACK |
| TCP-002 | 1.1.0 | tcp | high | Connection attempts rejected with RST |
| TCP-003 | 1.2.0 | tcp | medium | TCP retransmissions |
| TCP-004 | 1.0.0 | tcp | low | Duplicate ACK bursts |

| TCP-006 | 1.2.0 | tcp | medium | Established connection reset |
| TCP-007 | 1.0.0 | tcp | low | Slow connection establishment |
| TCP-008 | 1.1.0 | tcp | high | MTU / MSS inconsistency or path-MTU discovery failure |

| TCP-010 | 1.0.0 | tcp | low | Connection closed after a long idle period |

## TCP-001: Connection attempts receive no SYN-ACK

**Version** 1.2.0 · **Category** tcp · **Default severity** high

**Detection logic.** Group TCP conversations by server endpoint. Report endpoints where at least one conversation has a client SYN but no packet at all in the server-to-client direction. Conversations whose only SYN is within 3 s of the end of the capture are ignored because the answer may have arrived after capture stopped.

**Severity rationale.** High: the client cannot establish a connection at all, so the service is unavailable to it.

**Required evidence**

- Client SYN segments (tcp.flags.syn==1 && tcp.flags.ack==0)
- Absence of any server-to-client packet in the same TCP conversation

**Limitations**

- A capture point that only sees one routing direction (asymmetric routing) will also show unanswered SYNs.
- The capture cannot show whether the SYN reached the server; it only shows that no reply passed the capture point.

**Known false positives**

- Port scans and health probes to closed, filtered ports
- Captures filtered to one direction (e.g. 'src host X')

## TCP-002: Connection attempts rejected with RST

**Version** 1.1.0 · **Category** tcp · **Default severity** high

**Detection logic.** Report server endpoints that answered a client SYN with a RST and never sent a SYN-ACK in that conversation.

**Severity rationale.** High: the endpoint actively refuses connections, so the service is unavailable on that port.

**Required evidence**

- Client SYN
- RST (usually RST+ACK) from the server endpoint before any SYN-ACK

**Limitations**

- The RST may have been generated by a middlebox impersonating the server address.

**Known false positives**

- Scans of closed ports
- Clients probing several ports for an available service

## TCP-003: TCP retransmissions

**Version** 1.2.0 · **Category** tcp · **Default severity** medium

**Detection logic.** For each established conversation count retransmitted segments per direction (as identified by the Wireshark TCP analysis engine). Report a conversation when it has at least 2 retransmissions and they make up at least 1% of the data segments in that direction. Conversations are grouped by server endpoint.

**Severity rationale.** Medium: retransmissions add latency and reduce throughput but traffic still flows.

**Required evidence**

- tcp.analysis.retransmission markers
- Data segment counts per direction

**Limitations**

- A retransmission proves the sender did not receive a timely acknowledgement; it does not prove the original segment was lost (the ACK may have been lost or delayed instead).
- If the capture point is upstream of the loss, both the original and the retransmission are visible.

**Known false positives**

- Spurious retransmissions caused by aggressive RTO on high-latency paths
- Capture taken on a host with TSO/GSO offload producing misleading segment boundaries

## TCP-004: Duplicate ACK bursts

**Version** 1.0.0 · **Category** tcp · **Default severity** low

**Detection logic.** Report conversations with 3 or more duplicate ACKs (the fast-retransmit threshold).

**Severity rationale.** Low: duplicate ACKs indicate the receiver is missing data; impact depends on recovery speed.

**Required evidence**

- tcp.analysis.duplicate_ack markers

**Limitations**

- Duplicate ACKs also occur with packet reordering, which does not imply loss.
- With SACK, duplicate ACKs may be legitimate signals while recovery proceeds normally.

**Known false positives**

- Reordering on multipath links (ECMP / link aggregation)

## TCP-005: Receiver advertises a zero window

**Version** 1.0.0 · **Category** tcp · **Default severity** medium

**Detection logic.** Report each direction of a conversation in which the receiver advertised a zero receive window.

**Severity rationale.** Medium: the sender is blocked until the receiver frees buffer space, stalling the transfer.

**Required evidence**

- tcp.analysis.zero_window markers

**Limitations**

- The capture cannot show why the receiving application stopped reading data.

**Known false positives**

- Brief zero windows during normal flow control on slow consumers

## TCP-006: Established connection reset

**Version** 1.2.0 · **Category** tcp · **Default severity** medium

**Detection logic.** Report RST segments sent after the handshake completed and after payload was exchanged, where the connection had not already been closed with FIN by both sides. Severity is raised when an HTTP request was still awaiting its response at the time of the reset.

**Severity rationale.** Medium by default; High when a request was in flight, because users see an error.

**Required evidence**

- Completed three-way handshake
- RST after application data
- No preceding FIN exchange

**Limitations**

- Some applications intentionally abort connections with RST instead of FIN.
- A RST may be injected by a middlebox using the endpoint's address.

**Known false positives**

- Browsers aborting idle keep-alive connections
- Load balancers configured to reset on idle timeout

## TCP-007: Slow connection establishment

**Version** 1.0.0 · **Category** tcp · **Default severity** low

**Detection logic.** Report conversations whose first-SYN-to-ACK time exceeds 1 s (usually caused by SYN retransmission), or whose SYN→SYN-ACK time exceeds both 200 ms and 3× the capture's median handshake RTT.

**Severity rationale.** Low/Medium: connections succeed but users experience delays before any data is exchanged.

**Required evidence**

- SYN and SYN-ACK timestamps
- Handshake-completing ACK

**Limitations**

- Handshake RTT measured at the capture point only covers the path between the capture point and the server.

**Known false positives**

- Long-distance (satellite/intercontinental) paths with legitimately high RTT

## TCP-008: MTU / MSS inconsistency or path-MTU discovery failure

**Version** 1.1.0 · **Category** tcp · **Default severity** high

**Detection logic.** Report a conversation when (a) ICMP 'fragmentation needed' (IPv4 type 3 code 4) or ICMPv6 'packet too big' messages quote one of its segments, or (b) segments larger than 1200 bytes are retransmitted 2+ times with no acknowledgement while smaller segments in the same direction were acknowledged, or (c) a segment exceeds the MSS the peer advertised.

**Severity rationale.** High: large transfers stall completely while small requests succeed, which is hard for users to diagnose.

**Required evidence**

- ICMP fragmentation-needed / packet-too-big messages referencing the conversation
- or
- repeated retransmission of full-size segments while smaller segments succeed
- MSS options in SYN/SYN-ACK

**Limitations**

- If ICMP is filtered before the capture point, only the retransmission pattern (b) is visible.
- TSO/GRO on the capture host can show segments larger than the MSS; check where the capture was taken.

**Known false positives**

- Captures taken on a host with segmentation offload (large 'super-segments')

## TCP-009: Only one direction of the conversation is visible

**Version** 1.1.0 · **Category** tcp · **Default severity** medium

**Detection logic.** Report conversations with traffic from one side only in which that side acknowledges data from the other side (its ACK number advances), proving the other side's packets exist but were not captured.

**Severity rationale.** Medium: asymmetric paths break stateful devices (firewalls, load balancers without SNAT) and also limit what this capture can prove.

**Required evidence**

- Packets in only one direction
- ACK numbers acknowledging data that never crossed the capture point

**Limitations**

- Cannot tell whether the missing direction takes a different network path or was filtered by the capture tool.

**Known false positives**

- Capture filters such as 'src host X'
- SPAN sessions configured for one direction only

## TCP-010: Connection closed after a long idle period

**Version** 1.0.0 · **Category** tcp · **Default severity** low

**Detection logic.** Report conversations whose largest idle gap is at least 30 s and whose next packet after the gap is a RST or FIN.

**Severity rationale.** Low: timeouts are often intended, but mismatched timeouts cause intermittent errors on reused connections.

**Required evidence**

- Inter-packet gap of 30 s or more
- RST or FIN as the first packet after the gap

**Limitations**

- The capture shows the timing pattern only; the device enforcing the timeout must be confirmed from its configuration.

**Known false positives**

- Applications that deliberately close idle connections

## TCP-011: SYN-ACK sent but handshake never completes

**Version** 1.0.0 · **Category** tcp · **Default severity** high

**Detection logic.** Report conversations with at least one SYN-ACK, no handshake-completing ACK and no client data.

**Severity rationale.** High: the server accepted the connection but the client never learns of it, so the connection fails.

**Required evidence**

- SYN-ACK from server (often retransmitted)
- No final ACK from the client

**Limitations**

- If the capture is on the server, it cannot show whether the SYN-ACK reached the client.

**Known false positives**

- SYN floods with spoofed sources (many sources, one SYN each)

## TLS-001: TLS alert terminates the handshake

**Version** 1.2.0 · **Category** tls · **Default severity** high

**Detection logic.** Report fatal alerts and non-close_notify warning alerts seen before the first application-data record of the conversation. Group by server endpoint, alert description and sending side.

**Severity rationale.** High: a fatal alert during the handshake means no application data can be exchanged.

**Required evidence**

- Cleartext TLS alert record (content type 21) sent before any application data

**Limitations**

- TLS 1.3 encrypts alerts sent after the ServerHello; those are not visible without decryption keys.
- The alert name states the sender's reason category, not the exact configuration problem.

**Known false positives**

- Clients probing protocol support (e.g. scanners) intentionally triggering alerts

## TLS-002: ClientHello not answered

**Version** 1.0.0 · **Category** tls · **Default severity** high

**Detection logic.** Report conversations where a ClientHello was sent, no ServerHello or alert followed, and the conversation was closed (FIN/RST) or went silent for at least 3 s before capture end.

**Severity rationale.** High: the TLS session cannot be established.

**Required evidence**

- ClientHello
- No ServerHello and no alert in the same conversation

**Limitations**

- If the server answered with something other than TLS (e.g. plain HTTP), it is reported here as no ServerHello.

**Known false positives**

- Captures that end shortly after the ClientHello

## TLS-003: Connection closed after ServerHello without application data

**Version** 1.0.0 · **Category** tls · **Default severity** medium

**Detection logic.** Report conversations with a ServerHello, no visible alert and no client application data, closed by FIN/RST.

**Severity rationale.** Medium: handshakes fail silently; may be benign pre-connections, so verify with client logs.

**Required evidence**

- ServerHello
- FIN or RST
- No application-data record from the client and no visible alert

**Limitations**

- In TLS 1.3 the failure reason is usually in an encrypted alert that cannot be read without keys.

**Known false positives**

- Clients that open speculative connections and close them unused (browser pre-connect)

## TLS-004: Legacy TLS/SSL protocol version

**Version** 1.0.0 · **Category** tls · **Default severity** medium

**Detection logic.** Report servers that negotiated SSL 3.0 / TLS 1.0 / TLS 1.1, and clients whose highest offered version is one of these.

**Severity rationale.** Medium: deprecated protocols are insecure (RFC 8996) and are increasingly refused, causing failures.

**Required evidence**

- ServerHello negotiated version
- or ClientHello maximum offered version

**Limitations**

- The ClientHello legacy_version field is used when no supported_versions extension is present.

**Known false positives**

- Deliberately supported legacy clients in an isolated environment

## TLS-005: Server certificate does not match the capture time or SNI

**Version** 1.1.0 · **Category** tls · **Default severity** high

**Detection logic.** Parse the first certificate presented. Report when the capture timestamp is outside its validity window, or when the SNI name matches neither the subject CN nor any DNS SAN (wildcards honoured).

**Severity rationale.** High: clients that validate certificates will refuse the connection.

**Required evidence**

- Cleartext Certificate handshake message (TLS 1.2 or earlier)
- ClientHello SNI (for name checks)

**Limitations**

- TLS 1.3 certificates are encrypted and cannot be checked without keys.
- This proves what the server presented; it proves the client rejected it only when a matching alert is also visible.
- Chain trust (whether the issuer is trusted) cannot be evaluated from the capture.

**Known false positives**

- Capture host clock wrong (validity is compared with packet timestamps)

## DNS-001: DNS queries without a response

**Version** 1.1.0 · **Category** dns · **Default severity** high

**Detection logic.** Match responses to queries on (client IP, client port, server IP, server port, transaction ID, name). Report (server, name) pairs with unanswered queries, ignoring queries sent within 2 s of capture end.

**Severity rationale.** High: unanswered lookups delay or break every application that depends on the name.

**Required evidence**

- DNS queries
- No response with the same transaction ID, client port and server

**Limitations**

- If responses return on a path that bypasses the capture point, every query looks unanswered.
- Resolvers may answer from a different source address (misconfiguration) which this rule treats as no answer.

**Known false positives**

- Captures stopped right after queries
- Queries to unreachable secondary resolvers that clients then abandon

## DNS-002: DNS server failures and refusals

**Version** 1.0.0 · **Category** dns · **Default severity** high

**Detection logic.** Group error responses by (server, RCODE) and report each group.

**Severity rationale.** High for SERVFAIL/REFUSED: the client receives no usable answer.

**Required evidence**

- DNS responses with RCODE SERVFAIL(2), REFUSED(5), FORMERR(1) or NOTIMP(4)

**Limitations**

- The capture does not show which upstream step failed inside the resolver.

**Known false positives**

- DNSSEC validation failures for deliberately broken test zones

## DNS-003: Names that do not exist (NXDOMAIN)

**Version** 1.0.0 · **Category** dns · **Default severity** low

**Detection logic.** Group NXDOMAIN responses by queried name.

**Severity rationale.** Low: usually expected; important only when an application depends on the name.

**Required evidence**

- DNS responses with RCODE NXDOMAIN(3)

**Limitations**

- NXDOMAIN is often expected (search-domain expansion, typos, malware probes).

**Known false positives**

- Search-list expansion queries (name.corp.example) followed by a successful absolute query

## DNS-004: Slow DNS responses

**Version** 1.0.0 · **Category** dns · **Default severity** medium

**Detection logic.** Report resolvers with responses slower than 500 ms.

**Severity rationale.** Medium: every connection to the name waits for the lookup.

**Required evidence**

- Matched DNS query/response timestamps

**Limitations**

- Latency is measured at the capture point, not at the client application.

**Known false positives**

- First (uncached) lookups of distant authoritative zones

## DNS-005: Truncated DNS responses and TCP fallback

**Version** 1.0.0 · **Category** dns · **Default severity** medium

**Detection logic.** For each truncated UDP response, look for a later TCP DNS query for the same name from the same client.

**Severity rationale.** Medium: if TCP fallback is blocked, large answers never reach the client.

**Required evidence**

- UDP responses with the TC bit
- Presence or absence of a TCP/53 query for the same name

**Limitations**

- A TCP retry may go to a different resolver than the one captured.

**Known false positives**

- Large DNSSEC/TXT answers where truncation is expected

## HTTP-001: HTTP 5xx server errors

**Version** 1.1.0 · **Category** http · **Default severity** high

**Detection logic.** Group 5xx responses by server endpoint and Host header.

**Severity rationale.** High: users receive an error page instead of content.

**Required evidence**

- Cleartext (or decrypted) HTTP responses with status 500-599

**Limitations**

- Encrypted HTTPS traffic is only covered when decryption material was supplied.

**Known false positives**

- Planned maintenance pages returned with 503

## HTTP-002: Slow HTTP responses

**Version** 1.1.0 · **Category** http · **Default severity** medium

**Detection logic.** Report requests whose response took more than 2 s. The time to first byte (TTFB) separates server think-time from transfer time.

**Severity rationale.** Medium: users wait; the service still responds.

**Required evidence**

- Request timestamp
- First response byte timestamp
- Response completion timestamp

**Limitations**

- Response time is measured to the frame where the HTTP dissector completed the response, which for large bodies is the last segment.

**Known false positives**

- Long-polling or streaming endpoints
- Large downloads

## HTTP-003: HTTP requests without a response

**Version** 1.0.0 · **Category** http · **Default severity** high

**Detection logic.** Report requests with no matching response where the connection was later closed, or the request is older than 3 s at capture end.

**Severity rationale.** High: the client never receives an answer.

**Required evidence**

- HTTP request
- Connection closed (FIN/RST) or idle until capture end without a response

**Limitations**

- HTTP pipelining with out-of-order failures may misattribute responses.

**Known false positives**

- Capture stopped while a long request was still being processed

## HTTP-004: Response consistent with security-policy blocking (ASM/AWAF)

**Version** 1.0.0 · **Category** f5 · **Default severity** medium

**Detection logic.** Detect the ASM/AWAF default blocking page ('The requested URL was rejected...') and extract its support ID; separately report 403 responses that set TS* cookies.

**Severity rationale.** Medium: legitimate users may be blocked (false positive policy), or the block may be correct.

**Required evidence**

- Cleartext HTTP response containing the BIG-IP ASM default blocking page text, or
- 403 response carrying ASM-style TS cookies

**Limitations**

- A packet capture cannot establish the exact ASM/AWAF violation, policy decision or APM session failure; confirm with BIG-IP ASM request logs / APM session logs and the relevant policy configuration.
- Custom blocking pages are not recognised unless they keep the default text.

**Known false positives**

- Applications that copy the default ASM blocking text
- 403 from the application with unrelated TS* cookies

## HTTP-005: Repeated authentication redirects or challenges (APM / SSO)

**Version** 1.0.0 · **Category** f5 · **Default severity** medium

**Detection logic.** Per client and server, count redirects grouped by Location and 401 challenges. Mark APM involvement only when APM cookie names (MRHSession, LastMRH_Session, F5_ST...) or APM paths (/my.policy, /vdesk/) are visible.

**Severity rationale.** Medium: users cannot log in or are repeatedly prompted.

**Required evidence**

- Three or more redirects (301/302/303/307) from the same server to the same Location for one client, or
- Three or more 401 responses with WWW-Authenticate
- APM cookie names or paths when visible

**Limitations**

- A packet capture cannot establish the exact ASM/AWAF violation, policy decision or APM session failure; confirm with BIG-IP ASM request logs / APM session logs and the relevant policy configuration.
- Redirect loops inside encrypted HTTPS are invisible without decryption.

**Known false positives**

- Normal multi-step SSO flows that redirect a few times before succeeding

## F5-001: BIG-IP reset cause recorded in the F5 Ethernet trailer

**Version** 1.0.0 · **Category** f5 · **Default severity** high

**Detection logic.** Group RST frames whose F5 trailer carries a reset-cause string by cause text.

**Severity rationale.** High: TMM itself states why it reset connections; non-idle causes usually mean failed requests.

**Required evidence**

- Capture taken on BIG-IP with 'tcpdump -i 0.0:nnnp' (F5 Ethernet trailer)
- 'tm.rstcause.pkt' enabled so TMM embeds the reset cause

**Limitations**

- Reset causes are only embedded when the tm.rstcause.pkt database variable is enabled.

**Known false positives**

- Expected resets (e.g. 'Connection idle timeout' on long-lived idle sessions)

## F5-002: BIG-IP cookie persistence behaviour

**Version** 1.0.0 · **Category** f5 · **Default severity** info

**Detection logic.** Decode unencrypted BIGipServer cookies (IPv4 'address.port.0000' encoding) into pool member address and port. Report each pool cookie with its members; raise severity when one client is assigned to different members for the same pool cookie (persistence not holding).

**Severity rationale.** Info normally; Medium when the same client is moved between members, which breaks stateful applications.

**Required evidence**

- Cleartext BIGipServer<pool> cookies in Set-Cookie or Cookie headers

**Limitations**

- Encrypted persistence cookies cannot be decoded.
- Decoded members reveal internal addressing; reports redact on export.

**Known false positives**

- Member changes after a legitimate member failure (persistence correctly re-balanced)
